articles.headline: Where NBA expansion stands ahead of the 2026-27 season
articles.description: As NBA training camps begin for 30 teams, here's the latest intel on the potential for the 31st and 32nd teams.
articles.headlineJa: 2026-27シーズンに向けたNBAチーム拡張の現状
articles.descriptionJa: 全30チームのNBAトレーニングキャンプが始まる中、31番目と32番目のチーム誕生の可能性に関する最新情報をお届けします。
articles.body:
NBA commissioner Adam Silver's news conference in December 2020 was remarkable for several reasons. Similar to many large gatherings during the depth of the COVID-19 pandemic, it was conducted entirely on Zoom. But it was also when he was first asked whether the NBA would consider expansion again for the first time in two decades.

The question, from then-ESPN reporter Tim Bontemps, was framed as a discussion of how the league might recover some of the revenue lost during the pandemic. Silver responded that expansion wasn't on "the front burner," but added that it was "sort of the manifest destiny of the league."

In other words, expansion was inevitable. The only question was when.

First, the NBA focused on securing its new 11-year, $76 billion broadcast deal. Then, it turned its attention to expansion. That process is now nearing its conclusion, with ESPN's Shams Charania reporting this week that the league is expected to select the winning bid for ownership of the Las Vegas team in the very near future, from among three finalist groups.

Here's our latest intel from sources around the NBA on how the final stages of this six-year process could play out.

Where does expansion stand heading into the 2026-27 NBA season?

Silver said he wants a vote on expansion before the end of this calendar year.

That's a broad enough statement to leave a lot of room for negotiations. As it stands, the NBA and strategic adviser PJT Partners, which is handling the process, are more focused on getting a team in Las Vegas, where the interest and bidding have been far more robust than in Seattle.

The expectation is the Las Vegas franchise will go for around $10 billion, with the winning group also expected to spend an additional $2-3 billion to construct a new arena.

As Silver mentioned, there is still discussion among current owners and the bid groups about the best place for a new arena.

A vote on the three groups bidding on Las Vegas -- Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; and Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo -- could come soon, sources told Charania.

The runner-up groups could then pivot to Seattle, where Kraken owner Samantha Holloway's group appears to be in pole position, with a valuation sources with knowledge of the process currently estimate to be around $6 billion.

Holloway has tremendous leverage because her company, One Roof Sports & Entertainment, has a majority share of Climate Pledge Arena, which already hosts the WNBA's Seattle Storm and the Kraken and could easily convert to host NBA games as well.

Any other bidder would either have to build their own arena or negotiate with Holloway to use Climate Pledge Arena, a state-of-the-art arena built in 2021, which has also hosted NCAA tournament games.

There's also a possibility that the runner-ups in Vegas will pivot -- as Josh Kushner and Bob Iger did in buying the Los Angeles Lakers from Mark Walter in August -- and try to buy an existing team.

articles.headline: Trail Blazers fire new announcer over past inappropriate posts
articles.description: The Trail Blazers hired then on the same day fired Braiden Bell as their play-by-play announcer after a series of inappropriate social media posts from when he was a teenager came to light.
articles.headlineJa: トレイルブレイザーズ、過去の不適切な投稿を理由に新アナウンサーを解雇
articles.descriptionJa: トレイルブレイザーズは実況アナウンサーとしてブレイデン・ベル氏を採用したものの、彼が10代の頃に行った一連の不適切なSNS投稿が明らかになったため、同日中に解雇しました。
articles.body:
The Portland Trail Blazers hired then on the same day fired Braiden Bell as their play-by-play announcer after a series of inappropriate social media posts from when he was a teenager came to light.

"The Portland Trail Blazers have zero tolerance for racist, sexist, or harmful comments," the team said in a social media statement Thursday announcing Bell's dismissal. "Social media posts made by our recently announced play-by-play broadcaster are in clear violation of team and league policies, as well as our values and expectations. Therefore, we will not be moving forward with this broadcaster."

Among the insensitive comments, as found by a reporter for KGW in Portland, were Bell saying he was "not racist" but "Asian people piss me off" and a number of misogynistic posts, including him shouting out "big girls" and "closet whores." The posts were reportedly made in 2012 and 2013, around the time that Bell was 15 years old.

Bell issued an apology on his X account on Friday.

"I am deeply sorry for the language that I used on Twitter," he wrote in the post. "These tweets, while wrong, were written by me 14 years ago while I was only 15 years old and have no reflection of who I am today. I do not take lightly any harm it causes now. I regret this being my first impression to many of you online, but I can take solace in knowing that the people who truly know me understand that this is not the kind of person I am. Again, I'd like to apologize to anyone who was hurt by my words and will continue to always treat people with kindness and respect."

Bell, 29, had been hired to call games after broadcasting for the WNBA's Phoenix Mercury and G League's Valley Suns over the past two years.

He was set to replace longtime play-by-play announcer Kevin Calabro, who had held the role since 2016 but left in July after what he told The Oregonian was a "subprime" contract offer.

"We did not meet our own bar in this process, and for that we apologize to Blazers fans and to Rip City," the Trail Blazers said. "We strongly believe that everyone who is a part of Rip City should feel welcome and safe and we will make sure that our new broadcaster reflects these values. We will do better."

New Trail Blazers owner Tom Dundon has made a number of cost-cutting moves that have come under scrutiny. Dundon also insisted over the summer that only public money should be used to pay for a $600 million makeover of the Trail Blazers' arena, the Moda Center.

articles.headline: RB Jadarian Price ruled out by Seattle Seahawks for Week 4
articles.description: The Seattle Seahawks on Friday ruled out running back Jadarian Price for their game Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers, as the rookie deals with a chest injury suffered in Week 2 and aggravated in practice Wednesday, according to Mike Macdonald.
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- The Seattle Seahawks ruled out starting running back Jadarian Price for their game Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Price is dealing with a chest injury he initially suffered in Week 2 and aggravated in practice Wednesday, according to coach Mike Macdonald. The team's first-round pick did not practice Thursday or Friday.

Macdonald said he isn't sure how long Price will be sidelined.

"By no means is this JD's fault or anything like that," Macdonald said. "This is just what happens in football. Unfortunately, injuries happen. He can't control these things. He's done everything we've asked him to do since he got here. He's had a great attitude. He's been a great teammate. He has a great future. He's going to play great football for us when he comes back, whenever that is. ... It's just unfortunate."

The only other Seahawks players with game designations are safety Ty Okada and backup linebacker Chazz Surratt (calf), who are both questionable. Okada was slated to start this season alongside Julian Love before suffering a hamstring injury that has kept him out of the first three games.

Love, meanwhile, is expected to play Sunday after missing the Seahawks' loss to the Washington Commanders last week with a calf injury he suffered in practice. He was a full participant Friday after limited participation Wednesday and Thursday.

Price has started all three of Seattle's games, though he was briefly benched against Washington after losing his second fumble in as many weeks. He has totaled 119 rushing yards on 28 attempts, plus 21 receiving yards on four catches.

Emanuel Wilson (109 scrimmage yards on 32 touches) and George Holani (102 yards on 21 touches) are the next two options in the Seahawks' backfield. Velus Jones Jr. is the top candidate on their practice squad to be elevated, as Seattle has done twice this season.

"I'm excited to see these guys play," Macdonald said. "It's unfortunate with JD. Hopefully this gives him an opportunity to get healthy, but we've got guys that are ready to go behind him that are preparing their tails off and are good players, so we feel like we have a good plan and we'll go play a game."

Zach Charbonnet is getting closer to rejoining Seattle's backfield. The Seahawks designated Charbonnet to return to practice on Thursday. The team's co-starter in 2025 is on the physically unable to perform list while working his way back from February surgery to repair a torn ACL. He has to miss at least one more game.

Charbonnet was listed as limited Thursday and Friday.

"Zach looks fantastic," Macdonald said. "There's a process to get him physically and mentally ready to go. We understand that, and we'll work with him and make sure he feels great when the time comes for him to come back."

articles.headline: 49ers WR Mike Evans a game-time decision with rib injury
articles.description: Niners wide receiver Mike Evans is questionable for Sunday, but said he's going to give "my best" to play against the Broncos as he deals with a rib injury.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans is questionable for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos and will be a game-time decision, according to coach Kyle Shanahan.

But Evans, who was a limited participant in Friday's practice after missing Wednesday and Thursday, said he is going to give "my best" to play against the Broncos despite his painful rib injury.

"It's my job," Evans said. "I take pride in trying to suit up every chance I get. If the injury isn't unbearable and you can't play through it, then I won't play. But if there's something I can play through, I'm going to be there for my team as best I can."

On Friday, Evans spoke to the media for the first time since suffering the injury in the first half of last week's win against the Arizona Cardinals. He said he wasn't sure when, exactly, the injury happened but on the play where he left the game, he was running a route, turned and then it "felt like somebody stabbed me in my chest."

Evans went to the ground and then slowly made his way to the sideline before he went to the locker room on a cart. Asked if he thought the injury happened earlier, Evans said he couldn't pinpoint anything other than a big hit from Cardinals safety Budda Baker, but he said he felt that in his head more than his chest or rib area.

While Evans' status will loom until closer to game time, he sounded like someone pushing to play. He said he doesn't plan to use a flak jacket because it "looks kind of weak" and it's more for quarterbacks. But Evans said a padding option will be important and he's hoping to use a compression shirt that has some built into it.

Evans said he has previously played through a rib injury. His game log shows that while he was a member of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, he had a rib injury in November 2022. He was limited in practice before playing against the Seattle Seahawks and posting five catches for 54 yards in a 21-16 win.

According to Evans, the key to playing through such an injury is getting adequate padding surrounding the rib while also making sure to take extra time to warm your body up before playing.

"It was brutal to play through," Evans said. "But it's something that I can do."

Shanahan, who recently dealt with three broken ribs from a car accident in July, also offered some hope that Evans will play against Denver.

"I would be out without a doubt," Shanahan said, laughing. "But he's definitely a lot tougher than me. So, hopefully we've got a shot."

Elsewhere on the injury report, the Niners ruled out defensive end Nick Bosa (calf), defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. (ankle) and defensive lineman Mykel Williams (knee).

Like Evans, linebacker Dre Greenlaw (quad) and defensive lineman Keion White (hamstring) are questionable after missing practice Wednesday and Thursday and then working on a limited basis Friday.

articles.headline: Fantasy football Week 4 inactives: Daniels, DeVonta to sit, McConkey questionable
articles.description: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
articles.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists. 

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 4 Buzz 

Week 4 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 4

Biggest concerns heading into Week 4

Players in London 

Keenan Allen, WR, Colts (groin): Allen originally appeared on the injury report as "having a rest day," but that was later changed to add an actual injury. That's concerning, especially for a receiver at Allen's age. While he was in play as a sleeper option this week, fantasy managers may want to play it safe and avoid this questionable situation all together. If you are going to risk it, make sure to wake up early Sunday morning to check his status.

Chig Okonkwo, TE, Commanders (hamstring): He has been limited in practice this week but is expected to play. Okonkwo has missed the last two games and, while it is encouraging to have him back, I would not risk getting him into your lineups right away. After all, he will likely be third in the target pecking order in a game started by a backup QB. There is some upside longterm though with Daniels potentially nearing a return. Okonkwo is a stash for TE-needy teams.

 Terry McLaurin, WR, Commanders (hamstring): Washington's top receiver was added to the injury report on Friday. It's scary timing for fantasy managers as that likely puts him on the wrong side of questionable. Stefon Diggs was already a strong start as both the top slot option for the Commanders and man-coverage target. The Colts have allowed the most yards to slot receivers and play man at the third-highest rate in the NFL. If McLaurin sits, Diggs gets an added boost in volume.

Players with early starts

Lamar Jackson, QB, Ravens (back): Jackson scared away fantasy managers when he was limited in Wednesday's practice due to a back injury. He has since returned to full practice and will play in Week 4. Simply put, never bench him in fantasy.

Zay Flowers, WR, Ravens (hamstring): Flowers started the week as limited before elevating to full participation on Thursday. He was once again limited on Friday and is questionable headed into Week 4. Flowers, who suited up last week, has a good chance of playing. He has earned must-start status as the clear focal point of the Ravens' passing attack.

DJ Moore, WR, Bills (shoulder): Buffalo's top receiver has been limited in practice and wore a red noncontact jersey. That's the same thing that happened last week and Moore ended up playing and seeing 10 targets. He no longer carries an injury designation and will play in Week 4.

articles.headline: Texans get WR Nico Collins (hamstring) back vs. Cowboys
articles.description: The winless Texans got good news Friday as star wide receiver Nico Collins is set to return Sunday from a hamstring injury that forced him to miss Houston's last two games.
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- After a two-game absence, Houston Texans wideout Nico Collins is set to return against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4.

Collins practiced Wednesday and Thursday this week after hurting his hamstring during a Week 2 practice.

The injury forced Collins to miss Weeks 2 and 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals and Indianapolis Colts as the Texans went 0-2. Without Collins, the offense averaged 11.5 points per game, but Houston scored 31 against the Buffalo Bills with the Pro Bowl wideout in the lineup in the season opener.

Coach DeMeco Ryans knows how vital the Texans' star receiver is to their offense and hopes he provides a major boost.

"Everyone understands and knows the type of player Nico is," Ryans said Wednesday. "He's an explosive playmaker any time he's touching the ball; any time he's on the field, he's a threat. Defenses have to prepare for him and they have to do different things to adjust for him, so we're happy to have Nico back."

Houston sits 0-3, and this week is a borderline must-win game for the Texans to keep any hopes of making the playoffs alive. The only time a team ever started 0-4 and made the postseason was in 1992, when the Chargers did it.

The winless start is disappointing considering Houston had Super Bowl aspirations. But 0-3 is where the Texans sat after three weeks in 2025 before finishing the regular season by winning 12 of their remaining 14 games.

Houston's offense also gets back starting right guard Ed Ingram, who missed the last two games.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Jadon Sancho willing to wait for January move
articles.description: Jadon Sancho is happy to wait to sign for a club. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Free agent Jadon Sancho is happy to wait to sign for a club, while Tomás Araújo is subject to interest from Manchester United and Chelsea.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Jadon Sancho is willing to hold out until January as a free agent before making a decision, if the right offer doesn't arrive before then, reports TEAMtalk. The former Manchester United and Borussia Dortmund winger is a free agent, following his exit from Old Trafford at the end of his contract in the summer. The 26-year-old has been linked with a whole host of clubs since, but is yet to make a decision on his future, with nothing advanced on his next club.

- Manchester United and Chelsea are monitoring a deal for Benfica defender Tomás Araújo, according to TEAMTalk. The 24-year-old is claimed to be on the radar of several Premier League clubs, but it's United and Chelsea who are most keen. Araujo, who can play center back and right-back, recently signed a contract extension until 2031, making an exit in January unlikely. However, with a release clause valued at £68 million, clubs could pursue a switch anyway

- Juventus are preparing a huge rebuild over the next year, with Tuttosport naming a whole host of potential transfer targets for the Italian club. In the goalkeeping ranks, Alisson Becker is claimed to be a player of interest, as he could leave Liverpool at the end of the season as a free agent. In defence, Oumar Solet of Udinese is viewed as an option, while RB Leipzig ace David Raum and Crystal Palace star Tyrick Mitchell are also on the Bianconeri's radar. Napoli stalwart Stanislav Lobotka, Manchester City midfielder Mateo Kovacic, and Real Madrid playmaker Brahim Díaz are touted as options for the central ranks. Meanwhile, Crystal Palace forward Jean-Philippe Mateta could be a striker arrival.

- João Félix is keen on making a return to Barcelona next year, when the Portuguese international's contract with Al Nassr is set to expire. articles.headline: Cucurella: Too soon to judge Mourinho's Madrid amid poor start
articles.description: Marc Cucurella has acknowledged Real Madrid have not started the season as they would have liked under new coach José Mourinho, but he says the team must be judged at the end of the campaign, not now.
articles.body:
Marc Cucurella has acknowledged Real Madrid have not started the season as they would have liked under new coach José Mourinho, but he says the team must be judged at the end of the campaign, not now.

Madrid have suffered two defeats in their opening seven LaLiga games, against Real Betis and Atlético Madrid, leaving them six points behind early leaders Barcelona.

- Torres forced out of Spain squad; Madrid's Espí gets 1st call-up

- De la Fuente says beloved Yamal puts 'magic' at service of Spain

- UEFA receives Madrid dossier on Barça-Negreira case

Cucurella, speaking in a news conference on Friday while on international duty with world champions Spain, said Madrid's new project needs time to take shape.

"It's all a process," Cucurella said. "With the national team, the foundations have been laid over many years -- with the [same] coach, too.

"At Madrid, we have just started with a new manager and it's too soon to speak. Some players only had a week-long preseason before starting.

"The beginning of the season hasn't been what we all hoped for, but it's a process and we will see where we are at the end of the campaign."

Cucurella has picked up where he left off for Spain at the World Cup in the summer, impressing in UEFA Nations League victories over England and Croatia during the last week.

It has led to suggestions the left back -- a €55 million ($62m) summer signing for Madrid from Chelsea -- is better suited to playing for his country than his club.

"It's not even been 10 games yet," Cucurella responded. "There are things to improve [with Madrid], of course. We basically had no preseason, while it's a new club for me.

"I have to adapt to my new teammates and give my best so that the player you see with the national team is the same player with Real Madrid."

Cucurella's form for Chelsea and Spain not only prompted Madrid to sign him in the summer, but also led to him being named among the 30 nominees to win this year's Ballon d'Or.

He is also in the rare position of playing alongside two of the favourites -- Kylian Mbappé with Madrid and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal with Spain -- but would not pick between the two.

"If it was up to me to vote, I would vote for myself," he joked when asked to name his winner.

"But no, two of the candidates to win it are teammates, so who whoever wins it, I will be happy."

Cucurella and Spain are back in action on Saturday when they host Czechia in Oviedo looking to make it three wins from three in the Nations League.

They then close the extended international break with a trip to Croatia on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Miami Heat announce 'A Night in Vice City' theme ahead of GTA VI release
articles.description: With Grand Theft Auto VI's long-awaited release date set for Nov. 19, the Heat are partnering with Rockstar Games to offer a topical lead-up event the night before.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat have been carefully leaning into "Vice City" branding for years now, but 2026 will bring the team's most ambitious effort yet: Nov. 18 will be "A Night in Vice City" at the Kaseya Center.

With Grand Theft Auto VI's long-awaited release date set for Nov. 19, the Heat are partnering with Rockstar Games to offer a topical lead-up event the night before.

Miami is rolling out plenty of offerings for the night. The night will feature a special Vice-themed court and a reimagined edition of the team's popular alternate uniforms, as well as "special game night activities" and "unique game night activations."

According to a news release, the special occasion will "transform the Kaseya Center into Vice City -- showcasing the Miami-inspired setting of Grand Theft Auto VI -- for a first-of-its-kind sports crossover experience."

The Heat kicked off the promotion for the special event Thursday, lighting up "Welcome to Vice City" signage on the roof of the Kaseya Center. The team says it will share more information about "A Night in Vice City" in the coming weeks in coordination with Rockstar Games.

The Heat's game that night against the Milwaukee Bucks will be broadcast on ESPN.

articles.headline: New signing Carlos Baleba gets 1st Man United outing in friendly
articles.description: Carlos Baleba played his first minutes in a Manchester United shirt during a behind-closed-doors friendly on Friday.
articles.body:
Carlos Baleba played his first minutes in a Manchester United shirt during a behind-closed-doors friendly on Friday.

The 22-year-old signed from Brighton in a £70 million ($93m) deal in August but has not featured in a competitive game due to an ankle injury sustained in preseason with the Seagulls.

He did make the bench for the 1-1 draw at Fulham immediately prior to the international break and has continued working towards full fitness at the club's Carrington training complex.

Baleba took part in a training game against Swiss side Lausanne-Sport alongside fellow first-teamers including Harry Maguire and Matheus Cunha.

Head coach Michael Carrick told club media recently that Baleba was "pushing to get back as quickly as possible" from injury.

articles.headline: Erik ten Hag 'was a piece of crap' with Man United squad - Fred
articles.description: Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has accused ex-boss Erik ten Hag of being a 'piece of crap' when it came to squad management.
articles.body:
Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has accused ex-boss Erik ten Hag of being a "piece of crap" when it came to squad management.

The Brazilian spent five years at United, winning the League Cup and reaching the FA Cup final in the 2022-23 season.

Ten Hag came to United with a big reputation, having managed Ajax for four seasons and taking them to the Champions League semifinals but, while he did win the FA Cup and League Cup in his two-and-a-half years in Manchester, things did not quite go as planned with regards to success in the Premier League.

And Fred, who left the club to join Turkish side Fenerbahce during Ten Hag's tenure ahead of the 2023-24 season, gave a damning review of his time under the Dutchman.

"Ten Hag was tactically very good, but with the group he was a piece of crap," he said on the "Charla Podcast."

"He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano [Ronaldo], with Casemiro, with Rashford ... He wouldn't put me in to play, sometimes it got stressful.

"[With Ten Hag] Only his Dutch players played. A clique-ridden coach. But, tactically, one of the best I've ever worked with.

- Sir Alex Ferguson on David Beckham's Preston loan: 'He thought I wanted him gone but that's not true'

- Sir Alex Ferguson was 'terrified' about Old Trafford return after brain surgery

- Rasmus Højlund hits 'Siuuu' against Portugal: 'Cristiano Ronaldo will never be forgotten'

"He wanted the team to run, but Cristiano [was already] older. He took Cristiano out [of the starting lineup], and then there was a falling out."

Ronaldo left the club at the end of the 2022 season after he found himself no longer in the starting lineup.

Ten Hag was sacked in October 2024, with United 14th after seven matches -- their worst start since the 1989-90 season.

Fred also lifted the lid on other United managers he experienced, including Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the 1999 treble winner who took the helm at the club in December 2018 after Jose Mourinho was sacked.

The 33-year-old, who has 32 Brazil caps, gave his assessment of both of those managers, who he had much more positive things to say about.

"Solskjaer was good with the group, but he was helped [in training] by the assistants. He united the group," Fred added.

"Mourinho's a great bloke, he is funny. I've just been with him at Fenerbahçe; he brought me to United.

"Before [Carlo] Ancelotti came along, his name was being mentioned for the national team [Brazil].

"So I'd show him the rumours and he'd say: 'F--- off, mate. I'm not going anywhere. I'm going to manage my club here.' A really decent bloke."

articles.headline: Former Man City boss Roberto Mancini: Unconcerned by guilty verdict
articles.description: Former Manchester City manager and current Italy coach Roberto Mancini says he is unconcerned about being implicated in the financial rule-breaking scandal engulfing the English club, which on Friday said it was appealing the verdict.
articles.body:
ROME -- Former Manchester City manager and current Italy coach Roberto Mancini says he is unconcerned about being implicated in the financial rule-breaking scandal engulfing the English club, which on Friday said it was appealing the verdict.

In his latest comments on the issue, Mancini said: "It's not a problem that concerns me" -- despite appearing to acknowledge last weekend before a Nations League match in Turkey that he had "a double contract" as City coach from 2009-13.

Among the raft of charges that City has faced is an alleged failure to provide accurate details for player and manager payments between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

In 2018, German magazine Der Spiegel published evidence showing Mancini doubled his base salary of £1.45 million (now $1.9 million) for advising a club in Abu Dhabi.

City has been accused of potentially avoiding paying about £12 million ($16 million) in income tax and national insurance in relation to Mancini's salary, The Telegraph reported this week.

Mancini was asked if he was worried about the case ahead of Italy's match in France on Friday.

"No. I already spoke it about the other night. It's not something that concerns me. It's City's problem, unfortunately," Mancini said late Thursday at the Stade de France.

"It's not a problem that concerns me," Mancini added, repeating himself. "Look, really. I already said it the other day in Turkey."

- How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict

- Man City appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case

- Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more

In Turkey, Mancini said that "Manchester City is not guilty and the fact of having a double contract isn't my problem but theirs, probably."

Mancini led City to its first titles after Abu Dhabi's ruling family had bought the club in 2008, winning the FA Cup in 2011 and in 2011-12 coaching the team to its first Premier League title in a half century.

He was fired days after a shocking loss to Wigan in the FA Cup final in 2013.

City has protested its innocence throughout the long-running case, which reached a milestone Tuesday when the Premier League published a verdict saying the club was "guilty of all charges related to serious breaches" of the competition's financial rules from 2009-18.

articles.headline: Raphinha set to be fit for Barcelona clashes with PSG and Real Madrid - source
articles.description: Raphinha will be fit for Barcelona's double header against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid later this month after tests revealed no major injury to his right thigh on Friday, a source told ESPN.
articles.body:
Raphinha will be fit for Barcelona's double header against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid later this month after tests revealed no major injury to his right thigh on Friday, a source told ESPN.

Raphinha, 29, was taken off at half time of Brazil's 4-2 win over Australia on Tuesday after feeling some discomfort in his thigh.

He was subsequently removed from the Brazil squad for Saturday's game against India and flew back to Barcelona, were he underwent tests on Friday.

A club source told ESPN those tests had confirmed Brazil's initial assessment, that Raphinha "has edema in the thigh rather than an injury."

The news comes as a major relief to Barça after alarm bells were set ringing on Tuesday when Raphinha was taken off.

The forward missed 25 games for club and country last season due to a hamstring problem in the same thigh and there were fears he had suffered a relapse.

Despite the good news, sources say Barça will manage the player's minutes with caution ahead of some massive games in October.

Barça, who have won all eight of their matches this season, return to action after the international break on Oct. 10 against Getafe.

- UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case

- Clásico match ball for Barcelona vs. Real Madrid LaLiga clashes unveiled

- Transfer rumors, news: Several Premier League clubs eye Koundé move

In theory, Raphinha could feature in that game, but coach Hansi Flick will make a decision on his participation in the days before the fixture.

Barça then travel to Galatasaray and Real Betis before a huge week which sees them face PSG in the Champions League on Oct. 20 and Madrid in LaLiga on Oct. 25.

Raphinha has been a revelation for Barça so far this season, shining in a new role as the team's No.9 after the exits of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres.

He has netted 14 times in eight appearances, including back-to-back hat tricks in his last two club games.

articles.headline: Man City appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case
articles.description: Manchester City have confirmed the club have lodged a "comprehensive appeal" after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.
articles.body:
Manchester City have confirmed the club have lodged a "comprehensive appeal" after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.

The decision of the independent commission was published on Tuesday and detailed how City arranged "sham" commercial deals to inflate revenues and reduce costs by £900 million ($1.2b billion) during a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

The club have branded the verdict "unsafe." City announced their appeal in a statement posted on their official website on Friday.

It read: "Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday, October 1 2026 the club lodged its comprehensive appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter.

"The club's firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

- How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict

- Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more

- Downing Street clarifies Andy Burnham's remarks on Man City case

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case."

The Premier League confirmed that City "lodged the appeal to the Chair of the Judicial Panel" and that "the independent Appeal Board hearing will remain private and confidential until publication of the outcome is permitted."

Fines, points deductions and other sporting sanctions are among "a broad discretion" of sanctions available to the commission, the Premier League also said.

The Appeal Board, appointed by the Chair of the Judicial Panel, "must have three members, one of whom should have held judicial office, and would sit as the chair of the Appeal Board," their statement on Friday added.

In their previous statement on Tuesday, the Premier League called for any appeal to be "concluded as soon as possible."

Immediately following the publication of the independent commission's findings on Tuesday, City CEO Ferran Soriano sent a video message to staff insisting the club are innocent.

He said: "The whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation -- that the owners' personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true."

Sources have told ESPN that part of City's appeal is expected to claim that the money in question came from the Abu Dhabi government rather than the club's owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG).

The argument is likely to raise questions about whether City are privately-owned -- which the club has maintained since the takeover in 2008 -- or owned by the state of Abu Dhabi.
